## Coffee Shop Weekly Dashboard Overview

A compact dashboard for this dataset should focus on **sales volume**, **channel mix**, and **order efficiency**. Since the data covers only 3 days, the charts should be designed to roll into a weekly view as more days are added.

## Three Best Charts for the Dashboard

### 1) Revenue Trend by Day and Channel
Show how revenue changes across days, split by **store** and **delivery**.

- **Chart type:** Grouped bar chart or stacked column chart
- **X-axis:** Date
- **Y-axis:** Revenue
- **Series:** Store, Delivery
- **What it shows:** Which channel drives most revenue each day, and whether performance is rising or falling
- **Why it helps:** Quickly reveals the stronger revenue channel and daily swings

### 2) Orders Trend by Day and Channel
Show how many orders came in each day, separated by channel.

- **Chart type:** Grouped bar chart
- **X-axis:** Date
- **Y-axis:** Orders
- **Series:** Store, Delivery
- **What it shows:** Demand patterns by channel and day
- **Why it helps:** Helps the owner see whether revenue changes are driven by more orders or higher order value

### 3) Average Order Value by Channel
Show how much revenue each order generates in each channel.

- **Chart type:** Bar chart
- **X-axis:** Channel
- **Y-axis:** Average order value
- **Calculation:** Revenue ÷ Orders
- **What it shows:** Store vs delivery basket size
- **Why it helps:** Highlights which channel is more profitable per order and where upselling may matter

## Chart Data to Use

| Metric | Store | Delivery |
|---|---:|---:|
| Total Revenue | 3,735 | 1,255 |
| Total Orders | 250 | 64 |
| Average Order Value | 14.94 | 19.61 |

| Date | Store Revenue | Delivery Revenue | Store Orders | Delivery Orders |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2026-01-01 | 1,240 | 410 | 83 | 21 |
| 2026-01-02 | 1,315 | 455 | 88 | 24 |
| 2026-01-03 | 1,180 | 390 | 79 | 19 |

## Two Actionable Insights

- **Store is the main revenue engine:** Store generated about **75% of total revenue** and nearly **80% of all orders**, so staffing, stock, and peak-hour readiness should prioritize in-store demand.
- **Delivery has higher order value:** Delivery averages about **19.61 per order** vs **14.94** in-store, which suggests delivery customers spend more per ticket and may respond well to bundles, add-ons, or minimum-order incentives.
